sentences.text: Good morning.
How are you, Andy?
Yeah, good.
I'm really sorry I'm late.
Client call, you know, it's before you and it's Friday, isn't it?
Friday.
Friday afternoon in the uk.
So, yeah, it was a bit more jolly than, than usual.
You got any good plans this weekend?
Sorry?
Any good plans this weekend?
I haven't got any plans, but that's a good thing because normally, normally I've got tons to do, but my youngest one, who's 10, has, has a weekend all booked up and sleepovers and stuff.
So actually I've got a weekend of nothing planned for myself, which is great.
That's great.
That's awesome.

So I just wanted to jump on a quick call sort of in between, you know, any further calls that you might want to have just to see where you guys are and maybe if there's any like, you know, off the record questions that you wanted to ask that maybe feel a bit too awkward to ask Jeff or, or anything really.
Just, you know, how did you feel it went?
The conversation?
Are you feeling positive or.
Andy?
I'll, I'll jump in.
So we're generally interested.
We.
I think for us to really understand things would be a little bit longer of a conversation with the team.
I mean, quite, you know, the things that we're trying to wrap our heads around are, quite frankly, where, where is the, what I call the force multiplier for us in this thing.
So, and I don't mean financially, I mean from, for growing our share of the business.
So we join up and it's hovercraft, it's us and it's omm, if I have that right.
Is, is there, what is the investment from skyview to build?
I mean, for me, I'm, I'm trying to understand what the investment is to build a biz dev organization around it.
And if it's not it, if it's felt that it's not needed, then what, besides our hustle is going to.
What's the benefit to NextNow as far as bringing in bigger, better projects?
You know, is the concept that OMM is so connected and those projects will fall out of that into NextNow and we can look at, you know, obviously we're going to have growth goals for our P and L.
So I guess that's really kind of the biggest question for us, you know, what's the concept behind an investment in growing NextNow in our P and L?
Or are we just going to continue bootstrapping it and have some access to some of these other agencies?
Clients and try to cross sell them.
Yeah.
So I think the first thing to say is that they are work to bring more business in.
So certainly Jeff is a great sales guy.
I'm sure you can see that in him.
And he's looking to go out at the enterprise level and bring in more business.
Business that most agencies wouldn't have got, you know, at the level that they were at even, you know, you guys or hovercraft that they're looking to go out and get more business.
And one of the things that Jeff is particularly good at is going to the same company like a Nike, let's just say as an example.
But they may have hundreds and hundreds of different aspects to their business and most of the most agencies would only really deal into the sort of marketing level of that.
And Jeff is very good at going out and finding other parts of the business that we can also work directly with.
So Jeff is certainly going to take that in his hands and they're building out that biz dev team.
So everybody in the group is going to benefit from that directly.
So the natural order of things will be for them to develop more business for you guys and give it to you, obviously, because you are the experts in whatever particular area in the group.
And then in terms of I guess the sort of the concept to grow you guys.
Yeah, I think what they're not looking to do is acquire the business and then just leave you in a silo and see how you get on.
It's definitely they're looking to invest in the business to help you obviously increase margins and all of that other stuff.
I mean, Travis, which I think you might have met last year, but he's involved less in these calls now because he's got his hands full.
But Travis is very good on the operations side of things.
So they will be looking, you know, to find cost savings across the group with various suppliers, et cetera, et cetera.
So the margins are going to be better as well.
And plus, yeah, you'll be part of a bigger business.
They're well capitalized, they have investment.
They had several investment rounds before they raised capital to make the acquisitions.
So they have access to capital to put into the businesses and help them to grow.
And they've already reorganized both OMM and Hovercraft to help them develop business.
I think Hovercraft in particular is now a international agency and it wasn't before.
They're winning business in Europe and the UK already.
So they're looking to do the same thing with you guys.
And also I mean, they have obviously made two acquisitions.
They're about to make two small ones as well.
But it is still early days and they're looking for you guys to be involved.
You know, there's still seats on the bus, the sort of board management to bring you guys in and your ideas about where that can be steered going forward.
You know, I think as well, if, if you're having conversations with the hovercraft guys, which is, I'm understanding is the next step as well, they can speak to that more than I can.
But certainly if you have direct questions about, okay, what's it going to be like for us if we come in, do we get investment etc, how has it been for you?
Then they can give you honest answers about that.
It's all very fresh.
Yeah, I think that would be very illuminating, obviously, if we can make that happen.
And Andy, do you.
I'm trying to.
And, and I mean, these are conversations, I think.
I don't know if it's with you or if it's with Jeff, but I'm kind of curious about the, the scale of the existing organization and with the.
It sounds like there's two additional acquisitions that seem like they're, you know, on the precipice.
You know, what are we, what are we talking for, for revenue for the organization?
What, what are the go revenue goals like before?
You know, like I'm trying to figure out right now, are they at X amount and once we get to 100 million and blah, blah, blah.
That's one.
It's, that's when a transition will occur and Skyview will then put itself in the position of being acquired.

Yeah, I don't know the exact number that Jeff has in his, in his head in terms of revenue goals, but what I do know is that the value that you, you will be creating and bringing into the business is not all about revenue.
You know, in terms of creating the value for them to push the button for the exit.
It's more about what they're creating in terms of the business itself and the clients and the work.
I think Jeff said several times on the call about, you know, being the biggest and best known in the space.
That's what Jeff is looking to create.
And I think part of that is about reputation.
Not really, you know, being the only company that's doing a billion in revenue.
It's not, he's not really talking about that, but just more about the reputation and working with the best businesses out there and pulling them into the group.
But yeah, I mean, he can, he can tell you when he's.
Yeah, for sure.

That would be one of the, one of the next things that I think we would try to do is either meet with him in person or just get a more casual conversation on a zoom call, talk to, talk to our friends at Hovercraft.
And you know, I think it would be if, if we get to that point.
Let's keep chatting.
If we get to that point, if you guys could set that meeting up and let you know, I just want it to be clear.
I want them to feel free to share information, whatever is comfortable to share without me feeling like I'm pulling it from them.
Yeah, I mean they are extremely open with information.
So.
So definitely I can get them to share more.

My, my experience with them so far is that their process has been extremely open and they've shared huge amounts of detail in a presentation that they, they put together with an offer and they make their offers very early on so that everybody knows how it's going to work.
So the next steps for them really is the financials from you guys.
If they can look at the financials and they would be ready to put an offer on the table early.
And then we all know what we're talking about and whether it's worth investing in emotionally for the long term.
But certainly I can set up another call with Jeff, maybe Jeff and Travis to put on the table once we have some financials.
But the more immediate one may be just that meeting with, with Hovercraft, I think.
And it's like just, sorry.
I mean, I think it's great to talk to Hovercraft.
But I guess the details with Jeff and Travis, like some of the questions we had today.
Right.
Like, I mean, I think for us understanding the investment.
Right.
And maybe that's just part of each deal.
Andrew.
And you're.
You're going to educate us, right?
Like he talked about the deal structure in some capacity.
But if we're saying from our perspective it sounds like Jeff's going to build.
I like, I think for us we might be a little different than hovercraft.
Right.
Like we're somewhat of a sales focused in some capacity agency.
It sounds like the hovercraft guys are focused on the creative side, which we are.
Right.
But I think for us a missing piece is that investment in some key elements in our business to help us grow.
And I would like to understand.
Al, I'm sure you same thing.
Understand part of the deal is that structured in.
Prior to the, you know, us coming on board or After, I think we would want to understand, hey, you know, in our mind we need three account managers and a senior creative director.
Right.

And as you said.
Do you mean Randy just on that, do you mean.
Because obviously they wouldn't, they wouldn't invest into the business and then acquire the company further down the line.
They're looking to, to make a, an agreement on what the transaction would look like.
And from that moment, once everything is agreed, then yes, at that, that stage they start to invest.
Yep.
And I think we would just want, I guess have that conversation to make sure that we're aligned on, you know, from our standpoint.
This is what we see that's missing to get us to that next level.
Just make sure that there's alignment there.
You know, with Jeff and team, I.
Mean, I speak to a lot of agency owners and most agency owners are not actually that interested in building up a team of business development experts.
So I think Jeff, that would be music to his ears.
That is very much where his background is.
You know, his strengths are around the whole sales and marketing and business development aspect of things.
So he'll be really pleased that you want more of that over everything else.
I think they're looking to build a sizable business and if you're, if you're attracted by that part of it, you know, how can we get bigger within your organization?
Then that's the question that they're looking to answer for you for sure.
Okay.
Yeah.
I mean, Alan, I mean, is that aligned with kind of what you're thinking?
Yeah.
I mean, so Andy, just to like, just.
I'll say what Randy just said.
I think you got it anyway.
But it is important to know like we go after these three, three spaces.
Okay.
We, our experience has been that to win in some of these spaces.

I'll pick museum as an example to have a biz dev person, an account manager that is deep in the museum world, knows everyone in the space, goes to all the conferences, knows when a project is percolating, that kind of thing.
So that's really like, you know, for us, unless we're missing something, we're always willing to learn, our next step for our organization is to invest in those people.
And we think that's the low hanging fruit for next now to go from, to double and triple our revenue.
You know, like for us that's, that's the, that's what we see as the obvious is the Obvious thing.
Always willing to learn if there's a different way to do it.
But we're kind of looking at either bootstrapping that or finding someone with a growth minded mindset like Jeff and go how are we going to do this?
And is there a synergy?
Because there are more organizations.
So if we have this team together, it's not just selling us, you know, it's the Skyview thing.
So we're trying to understand, we're trying to understand if that is the, is the vision or if Jeff has so many personal contacts that he is, he is going to make the deals happen.
I think there's going to be an element of both.
Certainly he has loads of contacts and he's going to make a bunch of deals happen.
But also he is, you know, managing the, the rest of this process and busy with other stuff.
He is certainly the, the type to get his hands dirty.
But say he is also the CEO of the group and he wouldn't look at, be looking to make every sale himself.
So I think in answer your question, if I'm getting this right, they would help you build that team that you want to build.
I mean in, quite in.
When we say help build it, we mean fund it in some fashion.
You know.
So I lead the, the, the growth of that part.
Because he is particularly focused in the sort of sales.
Yeah.
Area.
Yeah.
I think he's looking to be guided as well.
I know that the hovercraft guys have pretty much been leading a lot of the, the you know, business needs conversations that you know, it's not just Jeff and Travis saying this is what you're having.
I think he's lent particularly hard on, on those guys more than the OMM guys, the management omm.
So it would be for you to make that play.
Really.
I think if that's what you're looking to do and that's what you're trying to get out of the relationship and that's what you want.
I think they would be all ears that you're looking to build up a biz dev team for yourself that is specialized in that way.
Okay, cool.
So it sounds like you are interested.
I mean I can't answer all of these questions.
Obviously I've got a big overview of what's been happening, but I'm not boots on the ground.
You guys are in Chicago, aren't you?
So I think that'd be, I think that would be doable for them to come over and see you guys and have a face to face, have a deeper discussion and I'll see how they are.
I think Jeff did mention particularly speak to the hovercraft guys as well, but in whichever order suits you best.
So we can start to set those up.
Yeah, and I think, like, Alan, I think we could chat and just say what makes the most sense.
Just, you know, obviously a lot of this stuff for us, confidential with the rest of our employees.
Like, it's just staying kind of within our walls.
So, you know, we know that our industry is small.
You know, we've had other conversations and grumblies come out to other employees.
It's just.
It's a challenging thing.
So.
So we do want to be mindful of that, you know.
Yeah, of course.
Yeah.
So let's.
Let's chat and then figure out.
Right.
Like, what makes the most sense.
Do we talk to Jeff again or do we kind of talk to the hovercraft guys and then kind of go from there?
So, Andy, can we follow up you later on?
Yeah, yeah, sure.
I mean, it sounds like you're happy to move forward.
So.
Yeah.

Your feedback on who you want to speak to next, obviously I can feed that to them, but from their point of view, we will need to request financials next, I think, because we want to get an offer on the table as quickly as possible.
And I think our books.
We were working on closing our books up.
We'll check back with our CFO on that stuff.
So they should be to a close point.
Andy, do you know, are there.
Is there a page one pager form of specifics of what you're looking for from a financial outlook from 2024 to whatever.
Can you share that with us again?
Do you have.
Yeah, yeah.

So they.

Okay, great.

Okay.

Yep.

I think maybe a 6, 7, 8 million.
Maybe 8 million.
Actually, I think it's around there in revenue.

Other way hovercraft, I think around eight.
Okay.

Okay.

Okay.

I think so.
A few other states that do it.
Okay.

I can double check with Jeff and I'm sure he's happy to relay the size of the business as it stands at the moment.
Okay, well, great.
Well, let us.
We also, you know, I think we got a couple more questions, but just want to get alignment just as we said today, probably with Jeff again.
And you know what, our thought process is just to be crystal clear on that.
And then, yeah, I think for us, like you said, I think trying to get a deal in place or at least an offer to say, hey, let's continue the conversation, I think makes sense.
So.
Yeah, yeah, I think so.

Yeah, I mean, these guys are really good.

I mean, they're good.

Great.
Yeah.
Okay, cool.

All right.
Yep.
Hopefully.
Thanks for your feedback.
I really appreciate that.
Thanks.
Cheers.
Bye.
I'll see.

summary.overview: The Exploratory Business Acquisition Discussion meeting between Next/Now and Skyview, led by Andrew Day, centered on assessing the potential for collaboration and acquisition. Initial greetings included casual conversation before Alan Hughes expressed interest in a deeper discussion about Skyview's strategic advantages, particularly regarding business development and revenue enhancement. Andrew Day detailed Skyview's approach to enterprise-level growth, emphasizing their commitment to investing in acquired companies for margin improvement and highlighting past successes like Hovercraft's international expansion. The conversation shifted to Next/Now's growth needs, with a focus on acquiring specialized personnel and resources. As the meeting progressed, participants agreed on the necessity of further discussions, maintaining confidentiality, and sharing financial information from Next/Now for the last three years, including budgets. The meeting concluded with defined action items for both teams, setting the stage for potential future negotiations.
summary.short_summary: During the Exploratory Business Acquisition Discussion, led by Andrew Day, participants from Next/Now and Skyview discussed the potential for collaboration and acquisition. Alan Hughes initiated the conversation by expressing interest in Skyview's strategic advantages, especially in business development and revenue enhancement. Andrew Day elaborated on Skyview's commitment to enterprise-level growth, detailing how they invest in acquired companies to improve margins, citing Hovercraft's successful international expansion as a key example. The dialogue then shifted to Next/Now's growth requirements, particularly the need for specialized personnel and resources. Both parties recognized the importance of maintaining confidentiality and agreed to share financial information from Next/Now for the past three years, including budgets. The meeting concluded with defined action items, paving the way for future negotiations.
